questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space and $\varepsilon_0$ permittivity of free space then the dimension for $(\mu_0\,\varepsilon_0)^{1/2}$ is :
questions.solution:
The speed of light in vacuum is given by the relation $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$.

Rearranging this expression, we get $(\mu_0 \varepsilon_0)^{1/2} = \dfrac{1}{c}$.

The dimensional formula for the speed of light $c$ is $[LT^{-1}]$.

Therefore, the dimensional formula for $(\mu_0 \varepsilon_0)^{1/2}$ is $\dfrac{1}{[LT^{-1}]} = [L^{-1}T]$.

Answer: $[L^{-1}T]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect for displacement current
options: Displacement current exists only when electric field changes with time
Displacement current produces magnetic field just like conduction current
Unlike conduction current, displacement current does not involve the flow of electrons through a conductor
questions.solution:
Displacement current is given by $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, which means it exists only when the electric flux or electric field changes with time.

It produces a magnetic field in the same way as conduction current, as described by the Ampere-Maxwell law.

Displacement current does not involve the actual flow of charge carriers (like electrons) through a conductor.

Ohm's law ($V = IR$ or $\vec{J} = \sigma \vec{E}$) is applicable only to conduction current, which involves the flow of charge carriers in a conductor. Displacement current does not obey Ohm's law.

Therefore, the statement that displacement current obeys Ohm's law is incorrect.

Answer: Displacement current obeys ohm's law

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Which of the following is an electromagnetic wave?
A. Sound waves
B. Alpha rays
C. Beta rays
D. Gamma rays
questions.solution:
Electromagnetic waves are waves that do not require a material medium for propagation and consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields. Sound waves are mechanical waves requiring a medium. Alpha rays consist of helium nuclei, and beta rays consist of high-speed electrons, both of which are particle radiations with mass and charge. Gamma rays are high-energy photons, which are a form of electromagnetic radiation.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave with frequency 40 MHz travels in free space. At a particular point in space and time, the magnetic field is $2 \times 10^{-8} T$. What will be the electric field at this point?
questions.solution:
The relationship between the magnitude of the electric field $E$ and the magnetic field $B$ in an electromagnetic wave traveling in free space is given by $E = cB$, where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum.

The speed of light in vacuum is $c = 3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$.

Given $B = 2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}$, we substitute the values into the equation:

$E = (3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}) \times (2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T})$

$E = 6 \times 10^{8-8} \text{ V/m}$

$E = 6 \times 10^{0} \text{ V/m} = 6 \text{ V/m}$.

Answer: $6 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electric and magnetic fields associated with an electromagnetic wave propagating along $+z$ axis, can be represented by
questions.solution:
An electromagnetic wave propagates in the direction of the vector $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

The direction of propagation is given as the $+z$ axis, which corresponds to the unit vector $\hat{k}$.

We check the cross products for the given options:

For option (FLnIo): $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$. This satisfies the condition for propagation along the $+z$ axis.

For option (v7vEs): $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$. This does not propagate along the $+z$ axis.

For option (Swd2S): $\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}$. This does not propagate along the $+z$ axis.

For option (pyQrQ): $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$. This does not propagate along the $+z$ axis.

Therefore, the electric and magnetic fields are represented by $\vec{E} = E_0 \hat{i}$ and $\vec{B} = B_0 \hat{j}$.

Answer: $E=E_0 i, \quad B=B_0 j$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with a speed of $2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. The relative permeability of the medium is 1 . The value of relative permittivity of medium is
questions.solution:
Given, $v=2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ and $\mu_r=1$
The speed of EM waves in a medium is given by
$v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}}$...(i)
where, $\mu$ and $\varepsilon$ are absolute permeability and absolute perimittivity of the medium.
Now, $\mu=\mu_0 \mu_r$ and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r$
$\therefore$ Eq. (i) becomes
$\begin{aligned} \\ & v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \mu_r \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}} \\ \\ & v=\frac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}} \\ \\ & \varepsilon_r=\frac{c^2}{v^2 \mu_r}=\frac{\left(3 \times 10^8\right)^2}{\left(2 \times 10^8\right)^2 \times 1}=2.25 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $3 \mathrm{~MHz}$ passes from vacuum into a dielectric medium $(\mu_r=1)$ of relative permittivity 4.0. Then,
options: Wavelength doubled and frequency remains unchanged
Wavelength is halved and frequency remains unchanged
Wavelength is halved and frequency is doubled
questions.solution:
The frequency of an electromagnetic wave is determined by the source and remains constant when the wave travels from one medium to another. Thus, the frequency remains $3 \text{ MHz}$.

The speed of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$. In a dielectric medium with relative permittivity $\epsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$, the speed is $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \mu_r \epsilon_0 \epsilon_r}} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.

Given $\mu_r = 1$ and $\epsilon_r = 4.0$, the speed in the medium is $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{1 \times 4.0}} = \dfrac{c}{2}$.

The wavelength in a medium is given by $\lambda' = \dfrac{v}{f}$. Since $v = \dfrac{c}{2}$ and $f$ is constant, $\lambda' = \dfrac{c/2}{f} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{c}{f} \right) = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$.

Therefore, the wavelength is halved and the frequency remains unchanged.

Answer: Wavelength is halved and frequency remains unchanged

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Column - I lists the waves of the electromagnetic spectrum. Column - II gives approximate frequency range of these waves. Match Column - I and Column - II and choose the correct match from the given choices.
No.Column INo.Column II
ARadiowavesP$10^{18}$ to $10^{20}$ Hz
BMicrowavesQ$10^{11}$ to $5 \times 10^{14}$ Hz
CInfraredR$10^{4}$ to $10^{8}$ Hz
DX-raysS$10^{9}$ to $10^{12}$ Hz
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic spectrum is categorized by frequency ranges as follows:

Radiowaves have a frequency range typically from $10^4 \text{ Hz}$ to $10^8 \text{ Hz}$. This matches (A) with (R).

Microwaves have a frequency range typically from $10^9 \text{ Hz}$ to $10^{12} \text{ Hz}$. This matches (B) with (S).

Infrared radiation has a frequency range from approximately $10^{11} \text{ Hz}$ to $5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$. This matches (C) with (Q).

X-rays have a frequency range typically from $10^{18} \text{ Hz}$ to $10^{20} \text{ Hz}$. This matches (D) with (P).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(R), (B)-(S), (C)-(Q), and (D)-(P).

Answer: (A)-(R) (B)-(S) (C)-(Q) (D)-(P)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What feature of the infrared waves make it useful for the haze photography?
options: Since it has large wave length
Since it is absorbed by the medium
questions.solution:
Infrared waves have longer wavelengths compared to visible light waves.

According to Rayleigh scattering, the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength, expressed as $I \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda^{4}}$.

Because infrared waves have larger wavelengths, they undergo significantly less scattering by atmospheric particles such as dust, smoke, and haze compared to visible light.

This reduced scattering allows infrared radiation to penetrate through haze more effectively, making it useful for haze photography.

Answer: Since it has large wave length

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency $20 \mathrm{~MHz}$ travels through a space along $x$-direction. If the electric field vector at a certain point in space is $6 \mathrm{~Vm}^{-1}$, then what is the magnetic field vector at that point?
questions.solution:
The relationship between the magnitude of the electric field $E$ and the magnetic field $B$ in an electromagnetic wave is given by $E = cB$, where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum.

Given $E = 6 \mathrm{~Vm}^{-1}$ and $c = 3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$.

The magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ is calculated as:

$B = \dfrac{E}{c} = \dfrac{6}{3 \times 10^8} \mathrm{~T}$

$B = 2 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~T}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of amplitude of magnetic field to the amplitude of electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum is
options: inversely proportional to the frequency of the electromagnetic wave
the speed of light in vacuum
proportional to frequency of the electromagnetic wave
reciprocal of speed of light in vacuum
questions.solution:
For an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum, the relationship between the amplitude of the electric field $E_0$ and the amplitude of the magnetic field $B_0$ is given by the equation $E_0 = c B_0$, where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum.

The ratio of the amplitude of the magnetic field to the amplitude of the electric field is $\dfrac{B_0}{E_0} = \dfrac{1}{c}$.

Since $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$, the ratio $\dfrac{B_0}{E_0}$ is the reciprocal of the speed of light in vacuum.

Answer: reciprocal of speed of light in vacuum

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Speed of electromagnetic wave in a medium having relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$ is (speed of light in air, $\left.c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$
questions.solution:
The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a vacuum is given by $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$.

The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium with absolute permittivity $\varepsilon$ and absolute permeability $\mu$ is given by $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}}$.

The absolute permittivity and permeability are related to their relative values by $\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r$ and $\mu = \mu_0 \mu_r$.

Substituting these into the expression for $v$, we get $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(\mu_0 \mu_r)(\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r)}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0} \sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}}$.

Since $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$, the expression becomes $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Television frequencies are of the order of $100 \mathrm{MHz}$, while radio frequencies are of the order of $1 \mathrm{MHz}$. Using these as typical frequencies, the ratio of the emf generated in a loop antenna by a television wave to that generated by a radio wave, if both have equal electric field intensities.
questions.solution:
The emf $\mathcal{E}$ induced in a loop antenna by an electromagnetic wave is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop, which is given by Faraday's law $\mathcal{E} = -\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$.

The magnetic field $B$ of an electromagnetic wave is related to the electric field $E$ by $B = \dfrac{E}{c}$, where $c$ is the speed of light. The magnetic flux $\Phi$ through the loop is $\Phi = B \cdot A = \dfrac{E}{c} A$, where $A$ is the area of the loop.

The induced emf is $\mathcal{E} = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left( \dfrac{E A}{c} \right)$. Since $E = E_0 \sin(\omega t)$, the derivative is $\mathcal{E} = \dfrac{A}{c} \omega E_0 \cos(\omega t)$.

The amplitude of the induced emf is proportional to the frequency $\omega = 2\pi f$. Thus, $\mathcal{E} \propto f$.

The ratio of the emf generated by a television wave ($f_T = 100 \text{ MHz}$) to that generated by a radio wave ($f_R = 1 \text{ MHz}$) is $\dfrac{\mathcal{E}_T}{\mathcal{E}_R} = \dfrac{f_T}{f_R} = \dfrac{100 \text{ MHz}}{1 \text{ MHz}} = 100$.

Answer: 100

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $30 \mathrm{~mW}$ laser beam has a cross-sectional area of $15 \mathrm{~mm}^2$. The magnitude of the maximum electric field in this electromagnetic wave is given by $\left[\begin{array}{l}\text { Permittivity of space, } \varepsilon_0=9 \times 10^{-12} \\ \text { Speed of light, } c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{array}\right]$
questions.solution:
$I = \dfrac{P}{A} = \dfrac{30 \times 10^{-3}}{15 \times 10^{-6}} = 2 \times 10^3\,\text{W/m}^2$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2}c\varepsilon_0 E_0^2 \Rightarrow E_0^2 = \dfrac{2I}{c\varepsilon_0}$

$E_0^2 = \dfrac{2 \times 2 \times 10^3}{3 \times 10^8 \times 9 \times 10^{-12}} = \dfrac{4 \times 10^3}{27 \times 10^{-4}} = \dfrac{40}{27} \times 10^6$

$E_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{40}{27}} \times 10^3 \approx 1.22 \times 10^3\,\text{V/m} = 1.22\,\text{kV/m}$

Correct option: (1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The correct arrangement in increasing order of wavelength of X-rays, UV rays, microwave is
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing wavelength is: Gamma rays, X-rays, Ultraviolet (UV) rays, Visible light, Infrared rays, Microwaves, and Radio waves.

Comparing the given types of radiation:
1. X-rays have the shortest wavelength.
2. UV rays have a longer wavelength than X-rays.
3. Microwaves have the longest wavelength among the three.

Therefore, the increasing order of wavelength is X-rays, UV rays, microwave.

Answer: X-rays, UV rays, microwave

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following waves are used to treatment of muscles ache?
questions.solution:
Infrared waves are electromagnetic waves with wavelengths longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves. They possess thermal energy, which is absorbed by the skin and underlying tissues, causing vasodilation and increased blood flow. This thermal effect is widely used in physiotherapy to provide relief from muscle aches, stiffness, and joint pain by promoting healing and relaxing the muscles.

Answer: infrared
